vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 3.0.0

The extract-memories skill is a utility designed to summarize and persist conversation context into a structured local memory system (memory/topics/). It uses session history access and file write permissions to maintain long-term state for the agent, following a well-defined schema for different memory types (user, feedback, project, reference). No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection were found in SKILL.md or the metadata.

llm.summary: The skill's requested file- and session-access aligns with its stated goal of extracting and persisting conversation 'memories'; there are no unrelated credentials, installs, or hidden behaviors, but it will write chat content to disk so you should review what gets saved and where.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (extract conversation memories to topic files) match the declared runtime actions and permissions: reading session history and reading/writing files under memory/ is expected and proportionate. No unrelated env vars, binaries, or external services are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives concrete instructions to detect conversation end (or use a heartbeat) and create/append topic files and update MEMORY.md. That stays within the stated purpose. Note: the heartbeat-based automatic trigger means the skill can run without an explicit user command and will read recent session messages — this legitimately supports the feature but increases the chance of persisting unintended or sensitive content if not correctly filtered.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest install risk. Nothing is downloaded or written by an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. The declared required permissions (FileRead/FileWrite/FileEdit and sessions_history) are appropriate for reading chat history and writing memory files.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default model invocation are set (normal). The skill requests the ability to read/write files in its own memory/ area and to read session history — these are expected for this feature and do not modify other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent, but it will read conversation messages and write them to memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md. Before installing or enabling autonomous invocation, consider: 1) Review the memory/ directory after a test run to confirm only non-sensitive items are stored. 2) Ensure the memory files are not automatically synced to external backups or VCS you don't control. 3) Decide whether you want automatic (heartbeat/end-detection) extractions or prefer manual /extract-memories only. 4) Verify the agent honors the 'What NOT to Save' rules — the skill can only follow those rules if the agent implementation enforces them. 5) If you handle secrets or private data in chats, restrict or disable this skill or add filters to prevent persistence of credentials, passwords, or personally identifying information. If you want higher assurance, ask the author for tests showing the skill's behavior on messages containing sensitive items and confirm a review step before writing files.
